NOTE: Anker 633 Magnetic Battery (A1641): Can charge most phones up to three times with a combined output of 18W (MagSafe wireless charging, USB-C PD, USB-A port). Features strong internal magnets and a fold-out stand. Kickstand is a bit flimsy. Prices observed at $40 (Amazon) and $42 (Walmart). [hands-on][expert-domain] (Source 1)
NOTE: Satechi Duo Wireless Charger Power Stand: Can output up to 20W and fully charge most phones up to three times. Can wirelessly charge two devices simultaneously. It's hefty and lacks magnets, but has a super sturdy phone stand. Prices observed at $100, $60 (Satechi with code CPTS14), $70 (Amazon), and $100 (Walmart). [hands-on][expert-domain] (Source 1)
NOTE: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim): Has a 10,000 mAh capacity, 15W total wattage, 1 USB-C port (input and output). Weighs 7oz (200g). Measured to provide 1.8 charges for a 5,000 mAh device. Features fast charging in a slim design and strong magnetic grip. It is heavier than expected and on the pricey side. [hands-on][expert-domain] (Source 2)
NOTE: Anker 10,000mAh Portable Charger (with integrated cable): Has a 10,000 mAh battery capacity. Features an integrated woven USB-C cable, an additional USB-C port, a USB-A port, and a front-facing display for remaining charge. Described as relatively compact and pocketable. Observed sale price of $22.99, down from $29.99. [hands-on][expert-domain] (Source 3)
NOTE: Anker PowerCore 10K: Has a 10,000mAh capacity. Features one micro USB port for input, one USB-C port (input and output), and one USB-A port (output). Can charge two devices at once. Anker claims it can charge an iPhone 15 twice, a Galaxy S23 up to 1.93 times, and an iPad mini 6 up to 1.23 times. Not explicitly reviewed by TechRadar, but the brand is recommended. Observed sale price of $19.99, down from $25.99. [expert-domain] (Source 4)

A.summary: For iPhone users in 2026, Qi2-certified MagSafe banks are the clear winners for convenience, while wired 10K banks remain best value. Hands-on testing from Wirecutter, Engadget, and TechRadar shows Anker's MagGo 10K line leads on speed, magnet strength, and real-world charges. Budget wired options with integrated cables deliver similar capacity for under $25 but lack magnetic convenience.

products.name: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K) - Qi2 Certified
pros: Qi2-certified 15W wireless charging faster than previous-gen Anker 633 per Engadget hands-on
LCD display shows remaining battery percentage and approximate time to full/empty
Measured 1.64 full iPhone 15 charges and 45-min half-charge in hands-on testing
Includes USB-C to USB-C cable and strong magnetic grip
cons: Weighs 8.82 oz, heavier than Slim variant at 7oz
Single USB-C port limits simultaneous wired charging
Pricier than wired-only 10K banks with no wireless
products.verdict: Hands-on testing by Engadget confirms this is the most well-rounded MagSafe battery, with Qi2 speed beating the older Anker 633 and a useful LCD. If you want one magnetic bank for iPhone 15/16/17 that actually hits 15W, this is the top pick despite extra weight.

products.name: Anker MagGo Power Bank (10K, Slim)
pros: TechRadar top pick for all-around power bank in hands-on testing
Slim design at 7oz (200g) with strong magnetic grip
Measured 1.8 charges for a 5,000mAh device
15W total wattage with USB-C PD in pocketable form
cons: Heavier than expected for slim label per hands-on
On the pricey side compared to wired 10K options
Only one USB-C port, no extra USB-A
products.verdict: TechRadar's hands-on top pick balances size and speed. The Slim is genuinely pocketable with strong magnets, but expert-domain notes flag it as heavier than expected and pricey. Choose it if you prioritize thinness over the LCD and extra features of the regular 10K.

products.name: Anker 633 Magnetic Battery (A1641)
pros: Wirecutter hands-on best wireless power bank recommendation
Strong internal magnets plus fold-out stand for video calls
Combined 18W output via MagSafe wireless, USB-C PD, and USB-A
Can charge most phones up to three times per hands-on notes
cons: Kickstand is a bit flimsy per hands-on testing
Previous-gen, slower than Qi2-certified MagGo models per Engadget
Bulkier than newer slim MagGo options
products.verdict: Wirecutter's hands-on testing still rates the 633 as the best wireless option for transit due to strong magnets and versatile ports. However Engadget notes Qi2 MagGo is faster, and the flimsy kickstand is a real annoyance. Good value at $40 if you don't need Qi2 speed.

products.name: Anker 10,000mAh Portable Charger with Integrated Cable
pros: Integrated woven USB-C cable eliminates extra cable to carry
Front-facing display for remaining charge
Additional USB-C port and USB-A port for two-device charging
Relatively compact and pocketable per hands-on expert-domain
cons: No MagSafe or Qi2 wireless charging
products.verdict: Hands-on testing by TechRadar highlights this as the practical wired pick: built-in cable, display, and dual ports for under $23 on sale. You lose MagSafe convenience, but for pure value and no-fuss iPhone charging via cable, it's hard to beat.

products.name: Anker PowerCore 10K
pros: Can charge two devices at once via USB-C and USB-A
Considered slimmest and lightest 10,000mAh on paper per expert-domain
Cheapest at $19.99 sale, Anker claims 2x iPhone 15 charges
Wide availability and reliable Anker brand
cons: Micro USB port for input is outdated and requires extra cable
No display or integrated cable for convenience

specs.ports: 1x micro USB input, 1x USB-C input/output, 1x USB-A output

products.verdict: Expert-domain coverage notes this as the slimmest/lightest 10K on paper and cheapest at $19.99, with dual-device charging. The micro-USB input is a real drawback in 2026, and lack of MagSafe makes it less ideal for iPhone, but it's a solid no-frills backup.

products.name: Satechi Duo Wireless Charger Power Stand
pros: Can wirelessly charge two devices simultaneously
Super sturdy phone stand per hands-on expert-domain
Up to 20W output and up to three full phone charges
Doubles as desk stand and power bank
cons: Hefty and lacks magnets per hands-on testing, poor for iPhone MagSafe
Bulky for pocket carry, not ideal for transit
products.verdict: Wirecutter hands-on recommends this as best for charging two devices at once thanks to its sturdy stand and 20W output. For iPhone specifically, the lack of magnets and hefty weight are dealbreakers for pocket use. Only pick it if you need a dual wireless stand, not a daily MagSafe carry.
